title: Spain's renewable sector has lost €140 Million to grid constraints as curtailment remains elevated since April 2025 blackout
gist: Wood Mackenzie finds Spanish renewable curtailment has stayed elevated since the April 2025 blackout, costing €140 million year-to-date, with nodes in Extremadura and Murcia losing over 25% of output. About half of curtailment stems from synchronous-system (voltage/inertia) issues rather than line limits, so whether curtailment stabilises or rises to 6.5 TWh by 2028 hinges on bringing 35 GW of voltage-control-capable renewables to compliance as ~10 GW more solar connects; batteries, data-centre demand and synchronous condensers provide later relief.

insights.claim: Spanish renewable curtailment has stayed elevated since the April 2025 grid blackout, costing the sector €140 million in lost revenue year-to-date in 2026 (Wood Mackenzie analysis of REE data, October 2026).
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Curtailment is a persistent, quantified revenue drag on Spanish renewable asset owners rather than a one-off blackout aftershock.
insights.locator: Renewable curtailment in Spain has remained elevated

insights.claim: Redispatch volumes in Spain's technical constraints market have not returned to pre-April-2025-blackout levels, with gas repeatedly called on to replace solar and wind output switched off for grid stability.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Constraint-market redispatch is a structural tailwind for Spanish gas-fired plant revenues at the expense of renewables.
insights.quote: Redispatch volumes in Spain's constraints market have not normalised since the April 2025 blackout
insights.locator: The finding comes from

insights.claim: Uncompensated constrained-off volumes in Spain stand at 4% of available renewable supply year-to-date in 2026.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Because the curtailment is uncompensated, the 4% hits renewable project revenues directly.
insights.locator: The finding comes from

insights.claim: At certain grid nodes in Extremadura and Murcia, curtailment already exceeds 25% of renewable output, meaning asset owners there lose a quarter of potential generation revenue.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: National averages hide node-level risk; asset valuations and M&A in Spanish solar must be done at nodal resolution.
insights.quote: For asset owners at those locations, a quarter of potential generation revenue is not being earned.
insights.locator: That national average conceals a sharper picture

insights.claim: About 10 GW of utility-scale solar is still to connect in Spain from October 2026 through 2028, part of a 16 GW wave over 2026-2028, much of which connected in the first eight months of 2026.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: More solar entering congested corridors raises curtailment and capture-price risk for Spanish PV before relief arrives.
insights.locator: Background

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie expects the next 10 GW of Spanish solar connecting into already congested corridors to deepen curtailment before it eases.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Near-term (2026-27) Spanish solar revenue forecasts should assume worsening, not improving, curtailment.
insights.quote: The next 10 GW of solar connecting into already congested corridors will deepen that before it eases.
insights.locator: "Redispatch volumes in Spain's constraints market

insights.claim: Spanish grid congestion that was once driven by wind supply is now driven by solar supply, because the grid was not designed for the pace or scale of Spain's solar buildout.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Solar-heavy portfolios in Spain carry rising locational risk relative to wind.
insights.locator: The structural cause is a grid

insights.claim: Solar-driven grid stress in Spain is concentrating around Madrid, Toledo and Cáceres as 3 GW of new solar PV comes online in those corridors.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Projects in these corridors face elevated curtailment risk; watch for discounts in asset transactions there.
insights.locator: Solar-driven grid stress is concentrating geographically

insights.claim: Developers are already siting new Spanish solar projects in lower-resource zones such as León, Valladolid, Huesca and Zaragoza to avoid congestion, shifting the investment geography of Spanish solar in real time.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Grid headroom is now worth more than irradiance in Spanish solar siting; land and grid-access value is migrating north.
insights.quote: a sign that the investment geography of Spanish solar is shifting in real time
insights.locator: Solar-driven grid stress is concentrating geographically

themes.theme: Voltage control, not line capacity, is the swing factor

insights.claim: Roughly half of Spain's technical curtailment in 2026 stems not from physical line capacity limits but from synchronous system issues: inertia, short-circuit current, and frequency and voltage control.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Half the curtailment problem is fixable with inverter configuration and grid-forming services rather than multi-year transmission builds.
insights.locator: The structural cause is a grid

insights.claim: Gas and nuclear plants provide inertia and voltage services as a matter of course, while inverter-based solar and wind must be specifically configured to replicate them, and much of Spain's existing fleet is not.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Synchronous generators retain system-service value in high-renewable grids; inverter-based fleets need upgrades to compete.
insights.locator: The structural cause is a grid

insights.claim: Around 7 GW of solar PV and 26 GW of wind in Spain, commissioned before Royal Decree 647/2020, require inverter retrofits to provide dynamic voltage control; up to 50% of the existing fleet cannot provide the service without further investment.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Creates a retrofit market for inverter and power-electronics suppliers and a capex need for older Spanish wind owners.
insights.locator: Around 7 GW of solar PV and 26 GW of wind

insights.claim: More than 35 GW of Spain's existing renewable fleet can provide dynamic voltage control at no additional cost, and compliant plants receive priority of dispatch.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Owners who bring plants to compliance gain dispatch priority, a cheap way to cut curtailment exposure versus peers.
insights.quote: More than 35 GW of the existing fleet can provide dynamic voltage control at no additional cost.
insights.locator: "Redispatch volumes in Spain's constraints market

insights.claim: Grid operator REE had habilitated 4.2 GW of renewable plants for dynamic voltage control through its habilitación programme by May 2026, a small fraction of the 35 GW that could comply at no cost.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Track REE habilitación volumes as the leading indicator for whether Spanish curtailment stabilises or rises.
insights.locator: Around 7 GW of solar PV and 26 GW of wind

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie argues that whether Spanish curtailment stabilises in 2027 or keeps rising depends almost entirely on how fast voltage-control-capable capacity is brought to compliance, not on grid congestion alone.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Regulatory compliance pace, not transmission build, is the key variable to monitor for Spanish renewable revenue risk.
insights.quote: Whether curtailment stabilises in 2027 or continues rising depends almost entirely on how fast that capacity is brought to compliance.
insights.locator: "Redispatch volumes in Spain's constraints market

insights.claim: If none of the 35 GW of Spanish renewables able to provide dynamic voltage control at no extra cost are brought to compliance, curtailment is forecast to rise 18% over two years, reaching 6.5 TWh by 2028 versus 1.3 TWh in 2023.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A fivefold rise in curtailment since 2023 in the downside case would materially impair Spanish solar and wind project returns.
insights.locator: If none of the 35 GW of renewables

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie's base case has Spanish curtailment stabilising in 2027 and 2028, but only if dynamic voltage control from new and existing renewables keeps pace with the ~10 GW of solar still to connect; otherwise curtailment targets face material delivery risk.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: The base case is conditional; investors should stress-test Spanish renewable models against the downside scenario.
insights.locator: If it does not, Spain's renewable curtailment targets

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie's Spanish base case excludes planned network development, so any grid reinforcement that materialises is upside to its curtailment projections.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: The projections are conservative on grid build; reinforcement announcements are incremental positives for affected nodes.
insights.locator: Background

themes.theme: Storage, demand and condensers as near-term relief

insights.claim: Grid reinforcement is the structural solution to Spanish curtailment, but a seven-year average lead time from greenfield to completion rules it out as a near-term fix.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Near-term relief must come from storage and demand, not transmission; position accordingly.
insights.locator: Grid reinforcement is the structural solution

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie forecasts Spain will have 10 GW of battery storage operational by 2030 (20 GW in the high case), up from a 2025 baseline of 0.2 GW, with over 40 GW under development and 25 GW holding grid access approval.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Spain is set for a ~50x battery buildout this decade, a major opportunity for BESS developers, integrators and suppliers.
insights.locator: Grid reinforcement is the structural solution

insights.claim: Data centre demand adds 2.3 GW to Spain's demand pipeline, with over 2 GW forecast online by 2030, helping absorb surplus renewable output.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Data-centre load growth in Spain is a curtailment offset and supports co-location deals with renewables.
insights.locator: Grid reinforcement is the structural solution

insights.claim: Renewables are expected to resolve half of Spain's enhanced contingency management problem, with synchronous condensers closing the remainder by 2029, after which curtailment is projected to fall 30% per year if conditions hold.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Synchronous condenser deployment is a key milestone; watch for equipment orders as a signal of curtailment relief post-2029.
insights.locator: Grid reinforcement is the structural solution
